title: Compact audit of main after the coding-guide restructuring, with the AUD-022 fixes verified

reviewer.name: Claude Code coordinator with five scoped reviewer agents and one skeptic agent per candidate finding

aud022Source.note: The tree of 870effe (a local object, not on any published branch) has the fingerprint that AUD-023 recorded for the source the AUD-022 remediation left. main's 8aa9b25 is 870effe with fixup commits of a cloud session folded in.

scope.summary: A compact ordinary audit at the owner's request for a short one. The review covered what changed since the source that the AUD-022 remediation left (`git diff 870effe ee4499e`: 335 files outside docs/audits, 182 of them in src): the coding-guide restructuring (TS-01 compiler flags, TS-03 checks instead of non-null assertions, the lint and code-rules gates, CORE-15 module splits), the SSKR crate's lints with its rebuilt WASM, a cloud session's changes (QR image limits, shared test helpers), the Windows raw-mode fix and oxlint 1.88.0; and it verified the fixes of all 20 AUD-022 findings. Code unchanged since AUD-022 was not reviewed again.  The coordinator ran every command once, one at a time, and challenged each candidate finding through a skeptic agent told to refute it. It then reproduced four findings with harnesses of its own (FUN001, API001, BLD001, BLD002) and ran the reproduction commands of ARC002, DOC001 and DOC002 itself; ARC001 rests on the reviewer's mutant run, repeated by its skeptic. Five reviewer agents had distinct scopes, made no change in the checkout and ran only single test files and small probes. Public fixtures only: the BIP39 test phrase, the README examples and vectors/.  Earlier findings are treated as a regression checklist through the verification of AUD-022; AUD-023 was started at 8de80e2 with the uncommitted remediation and never completed; this audit supersedes it at a new snapshot.

findings.title: Truncated share CBOR is refused as a fault of MnemoCode instead of an invalid share
findings.reproduction: `node docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/truncated-share.mjs` (five ur:sskr records whose CBOR is cut short and whose CRC32 is valid), or `node dist/mnemocode.js sskr-combine --share ur:sskr/hdrlprengr`.
findings.expected: An input refusal, as at 870effe: "Not an SSKR CBOR tag." or "Invalid SSKR share byte string.". src/core/defined.ts says a missing value is a fault of MnemoCode, never of its input.
findings.observed: Every record throws "MnemoCode expected a value that is not there: this is a fault of MnemoCode."; the CLI prints "Share 1 cannot be read: mnemoCode expected a value that is not there…" and exits 1. Commit bd4c948 (TS-03) replaced `cbor[1]!` and `cbor[offset++]!` by defined() on indexes that depend on the input.
findings.impact: The share is still refused with the same exit code and nothing is accepted; the message blames the program instead of the share. Reachable only with a crafted or badly encoded record, since a typo fails the CRC32 first.
findings.evidence: probe-truncated-share (exit 1, local log); sskr-export reviewer and skeptic probes against 870effe and HEAD (local only).
findings.recommendedFix: In sharePayload check the length before each read and refuse with the existing messages; keep defined() for indexes the code guarantees.
findings.requiredVerification: truncated-share.mjs exits 0; a test in test/sskr-boundaries.test.ts with these records fails before the fix and passes after it.

findings.title: The joint-repair entry no longer exports the types of its results after the CORE-15 split
findings.reproduction: `bash docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/entry-types.sh`: a host project imports ElementHelp, JointAssessment, MarkedElement, RepairedSet, RepairedShares, ShareAssessment and DIGEST_BITS from mnemocode/sskr/joint-repair.
findings.expected: The part's entry gives the same names as at 870effe; ARCHITECTURE.md and README say each part has an entry of its own that a host takes alone. A CORE-15 split is a move.
findings.observed: tsc fails with TS2305/TS2459 for all seven names. Commit b0cf85e moved them into joint-results.ts and joint-solve.ts, which have no package entry, and only imported them back. Public declarations such as RepairReport.repairs(set: RepairedShares) and ShareSet.unsettled: MarkedElement[] now use types no entry exports.
findings.impact: Compilation only: a host of the package cannot name these types (five can be derived from other exports); run-time behaviour is unchanged. The package is private and 0.1.0 unreleased; the multi-chain host compiles the synced sources and is not affected. A skeptic re-rated the reviewer's medium to low.
findings.evidence: probe-entry-types (exit 1, local log); sskr-export reviewer's export comparison of every entry at 870effe and HEAD (local only).
findings.recommendedFix: Re-export the six types from src/sskr/joint-repair.ts, and DIGEST_BITS or a recorded reason why it became internal; add a test that compares each entry's export names with a snapshot.
findings.requiredVerification: entry-types.sh exits 0; the snapshot test fails on the current entry and passes after the fix.

findings.title: code-rules passes a Python import that the script's existing requirements file does not pin
findings.reproduction: `bash docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/code-rules-gaps.sh`, case python-import-not-in-requirements: a script imports PIL and requests, and its requirements file pins only pillow with a hash.
findings.expected: TOOL-03 (Check: code-rules): every non-standard package of a Python script is pinned with its hashes in the requirements file next to it.
findings.observed: Exit 0. checkPythonPackages returns as soon as any candidate requirements file exists (line 249) and never compares its entries with the imports.
findings.impact: A script can import an unpinned package and pass pnpm check while it has a requirements file. No current script does: the four requirements files cover their imports.
findings.evidence: probe-code-rules-gaps (exit 1, local log); cli-build reviewer and skeptic probes (local only).
findings.recommendedFix: Read the requirement names (normalised) and report each imported module none of them lists, with a small map for names that differ (PIL to pillow, fontTools to fonttools, winpty to pywinpty); add the case to test/code-rules.test.ts.
findings.requiredVerification: code-rules-gaps.sh refuses the case; node scripts/verify-code-rules.mjs still exits 0 on the repository.

findings.title: code-rules misses Cargo dependencies written as tables or dotted keys
findings.reproduction: `bash docs/audits/AUD-024-harnesses/code-rules-gaps.sh`, cases cargo-dependency-table (`[dependencies.serde]` with `version = "1"`), cargo-dev-dependency-table and cargo-dotted-key (`serde.version = "1"`).
findings.expected: CORE-25 (Check: code-rules): every Cargo dependency is pinned with "=x.y.z".
findings.observed: Exit 0 for all three. The section regex matches only names ending in dependencies, and the key regex does not take a dotted key, so the version inside is never read; the inline form is refused as it should be.
findings.impact: A crate dependency added in table or dotted form with a range passes pnpm check. sskr-wasm/rust/Cargo.toml uses only pinned inline entries today.
findings.evidence: probe-code-rules-gaps (exit 1, local log); cli-build reviewer and skeptic probes (local only).
findings.recommendedFix: Treat a section `<dependencies>.<name>` (also dev-, build- and target-specific) and a dotted `<name>.version` key as one dependency and check its version; add the cases to test/code-rules.test.ts.
findings.requiredVerification: code-rules-gaps.sh exits 0; the gate still passes the repository.

findings.title: The --ask-secrets path of the AUD-022-SEC001 fix has no regression in the suite or CI
findings.reproduction: Change showOldPhrase in a copy of dist/cli/re-encode-command.js to write the phrase to standard output; the repository's three re-encode pseudo-terminal checks still pass (standard output and error are the same terminal there), and no test of re-encode-questions asserts that the old phrase is absent from standard output. Only docs/audits/AUD-022-harnesses/reencode-stdout.py fails, and no pnpm script or workflow runs it.
findings.expected: AUD-022-SEC001's required verification asks for redirected-stdout regressions on the options path and the --ask-secrets path; CORE-33 asks for a test that fails before the fix and after it is undone.
findings.observed: The options path has one (test/re-encode.test.ts:217-218); the --ask-secrets path is guarded only by the audit harness.
findings.impact: The fix is intact today (the harness passes in this baseline); a later change could send the old phrase to a redirected file again without failing pnpm verify or CI.
findings.evidence: aud022-fixes reviewer's mutant run and the skeptic's rerun (local only); reencode-stdout passes in this baseline.
findings.recommendedFix: Add a case with standard error a terminal and standard output not, asserting that the old phrase stays off standard output, to test/re-encode-questions.test.ts or to the pseudo-terminal checks with output sent to a file.
findings.requiredVerification: The new check fails with showOldPhrase writing to standard output and passes at the fix; it runs in pnpm verify or the CI terminal action.

findings.title: The permission-denied save message lost its only test when recover-word moved to the shared terminal
findings.reproduction: `git grep -n 'no permission to write' 870effe -- test` finds test/ask-word-recovery.test.ts:324; the same at HEAD finds nothing; `git log -S'no permission to write there' 870effe..HEAD -- test` names 1d4f97b.
findings.expected: A save that fails with EACCES keeps a test of its exact line, "… could not be saved as <path>: there is no permission to write there.", as at 870effe.
findings.observed: The shared failingSave helper throws only ENOSPC; no test at HEAD sends EACCES or EPERM through saveWithRetry.
findings.impact: A change to the permission reason, the usual one for a protected folder, would pass the suite; the behaviour at HEAD is unchanged.
findings.evidence: docs-tests reviewer's removed_expects.py and the skeptic's rerun (local only).
findings.recommendedFix: Let failingSave take an errno code (ENOSPC by default) and assert the EACCES line again; optionally one table-driven test over every SAVE_FAILURES entry.
findings.requiredVerification: A test asserts the EACCES line and fails when SAVE_FAILURES.EACCES changes.

limitations: A compact audit of about one hour: the review covered the changes since 870effe and the AUD-022 fixes; code unchanged since AUD-022 was not reviewed again.
No local Windows or macOS run; CI at a03862c covers their tests, pseudo-terminal checks and executables.
No local executable build or check; CI built and checked the three executables at a03862c.
No browser parity check of the multi-chain Deriver, which lives in another repository.
The pnpm verify:sskr rebuild ran with the Docker cache; no uncached canonical rebuild.
Reviewer probes and logs are kept locally (docs/audits/AUD-024-evidence/, ignored by Git); the three probes that reproduce findings are published in AUD-024-harnesses/.
The reasoning effort of the coordinator and the agents is not retained by the client.
informationalObservations: The rebuilt SSKR WASM differs from 870effe's in two bytes (offsets 228177 and 228193, 0xb0 to 0xb7), panic-location line numbers that the doc comments added to lib.rs moved; lib.rs changed only in comments, and verify:sskr reproduces the committed bytes.

withRawTerminal lowers its session count before the awaited turn of leaveRawMode: a later caller that started a raw session without awaiting the previous one could see raw mode left under it. No caller does so; lowering the count after leaveRawMode would remove the fragility.
docs/audits/AUD-015-harnesses/staging-probes.ts imports LeftStagingCopy, now LeftStagingCopyError (TS-06); it is frozen evidence but ships in the package and no longer compiles.
The TS-06 renames of public names (…Error classes, .problem and .kind to .code) are not in CHANGELOG.md; with 0.1.0 unreleased nobody depends on the old names, but a line would help hosts.

History before the release: main's 8aa9b25 is a work-in-progress commit to regroup, 45c9f86's message still says it is temporary and unsigned, and ee4499e is a fixup commit to fold (workspace Commits rules).
The AUD-022 records say the remediation is not committed; it is in 8aa9b25, and this report records the fix and verification commits. The AUD-022 records stay unchanged.

The multi-chain Deriver does not yet use RE_ENCODING_WORDS, confirmationLine or PNG_ADMISSION_SELF_TEST in its own host code, although its synced copy has them; the synced copies of the split files are byte-identical to HEAD.

ci.yml runs the full pnpm verify, the pseudo-terminal check, the card round trip, the SSKR replay and pnpm audit on every push, and executable.yml builds three executables on push to main; CI-04 asks for fast checks only on push. Unchanged since AUD-022.
Smaller gaps of code-rules that need no fix today: a second module after `import a as b, c`, `#!/usr/bin/env -S bash`, `long:` anywhere on a first line, and WEB-01 checked per line.
The CLI lowercases the first letter of a library message, which reads "mnemoCode expected …" for the message of AUD-024-FUN001.
test/aud-021-recovery.test.ts has three describe blocks with the same name; two header comments exceed 100 columns (scripts/verify-audit-privacy.mjs:4, src/core/png-admission-self-test.ts:3).
The CHANGELOG's bound of about 200 MiB for the PNG decoder was not measured again; the cloud session measured about 170 MiB.

remediationAddendum.statusRule: Fixed, not verified: the fixes are committed together with this record, and no later commit has verified them yet. Each test below was seen failing before its fix and passing after it.

fixes.change: sharePayload reads the tag bytes, the header and the one-byte length as input that may be missing and refuses a record cut short with "Not an SSKR CBOR tag." or "Invalid SSKR share byte string."; five CRC-valid truncated records are tested.

The entry re-exports ElementHelp, JointAssessment, MarkedElement, RepairedSet, RepairedShares, ShareAssessment and DIGEST_BITS; a type-level test of the test tsconfig fails when one goes missing (seven errors without the fix).

checkPythonPackages reads the existing requirements files and reports each imported package that none pins, by its published name (PIL, fontTools and winpty mapped) compared as pip compares names; one parser of requirement entries serves both checks.

checkCargoManifest collects each dependency of a section in any TOML form (string, inline table, dotted keys, its own table, dev-, build- and target-specific) and checks its version when the section ends.

re-encode --ask-secrets with standard output not a terminal: the new backup on standard output, no word of the old phrase there, the phrase on standard error only when it is a terminal; both cases fail with showOldPhrase writing to standard output.

failingSave takes the errno code of its failures (ENOSPC unless a test names another); recover-word asserts the exact EACCES line again and the off-screen EPERM rejection; a changed EACCES text fails the test.
The host contract names code: "unsupported" and code: "damaged".
The paragraph points to the table, whose rows link every harness folder.
